concepts.title: Meaning and Need for a Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Need for a Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: A constitution is the supreme law of a country that defines the basic political structure, distributes powers among organs of government, and lays down the fundamental rights and duties of citizens and the state.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Need for a Constitution'.
questions.a: A constitution provides the legal and moral framework for governance, ensuring that power is exercised within defined limits and that the rights of citizens are protected.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Need for a Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Why Do We Need a Constitution?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functions of a Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The functions of a constitution include establishing a framework of government, distributing powers among organs, limiting government power, expressing the identity of the nation, and protecting the rights of citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functions of a Constitution'.
questions.a: A constitution both empowers the government to act and limits its power, while also defining the nation's identity and guaranteeing citizens' rights.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Functions of a Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Functions of a Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Constitutions' refers to.
questions.a: Constitutions are classified as written or unwritten, rigid or flexible, and unitary or federal based on whether they are codified in a single document, the difficulty of amendment, and the distribution of power between central and regional governments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Constitutions'.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution is written, partly rigid and partly flexible, and federal in structure with unitary features, combining elements from different constitutional types.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Constitutions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Constitutions

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Making of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution was drafted by the Constituent Assembly between December 1946 and November 1949, drawing on the Government of India Act 1935, other constitutions, and the reports of various committees, and was adopted on 26 November 1949.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Making of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution was made by a representative Constituent Assembly through deliberation, borrowing useful provisions from world constitutions, and adapting them to Indian conditions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Making of the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Making of the Indian Constitution

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Constituent Assembly' refers to.
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly was the body of elected representatives that deliberated and drafted the Indian Constitution, first meeting on 9 December 1946, with 389 members initially and 299 after partition, representing provinces and princely states.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Constituent Assembly'.
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly was a representative and deliberative body that reflected the diversity of India and worked through committees and detailed debates to produce the Constitution.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Constituent Assembly' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Constituent Assembly

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Constitutional Amendments' refers to.
questions.a: A constitutional amendment is a formal change or addition to the provisions of the constitution, made to keep it updated with changing times while preserving its basic structure, through procedures laid down in Article 368 of the Indian Constitution.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Constitutional Amendments'.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution can be amended by Parliament through different procedures depending on the nature of the provision, ranging from simple majority to special majority with ratification by half the States.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Constitutional Amendments' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Constitutional Amendments

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Basic Structure Doctrine' refers to.
questions.a: The basic structure doctrine is a judicial principle established in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) which holds that Parliament cannot amend the basic structure or essential features of the Constitution, even under its amending power under Article 368.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Basic Structure Doctrine'.
questions.a: The Supreme Court established that while Parliament can amend the Constitution, it cannot destroy or damage its basic structure, thus protecting the identity and core principles of the Constitution.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Basic Structure Doctrine' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Basic Structure Doctrine

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sources of the Indian Constitution' refers to.
questions.a: The Indian Constitution drew provisions from various sources including the Government of India Act 1935, the British Constitution, the US Constitution, the Irish Constitution, the Canadian Constitution, and the Australian Constitution, adapting them to Indian needs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sources of the Indian Constitution'.
questions.a: The makers of the Indian Constitution borrowed suitable features from constitutions around the world and adapted them to Indian conditions, creating a unique blend of borrowed and indigenous provisions.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sources of the Indian Constitution' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sources of the Indian Constitution
